description: Provider-neutral example alert rules for the pdf.xyz secure-worker SLOs (Phase 28). One rule per SLO indicator; thresholds mirror DEFAULT_SLO_THRESHOLDS in src/lib/workers/observability/slo.ts and are a STARTING POINT an operator tunes to their traffic. Content-free by construction: every rule references only a bounded SLO id, a severity, a duration, and generic prose — no endpoint, host, bucket, object key, filename, secret, or user data. `severity` is one of page | ticket | warn.

rules.summary: Worker job completion success rate has fallen below its SLO (completed / (completed + failed)).
Compression processor success rate is below its SLO; inspect executor error codes and engine health.
OCR processor success rate is below its SLO; check the OCR engine readiness on the worker image.
p95 processor latency exceeds its SLO (histogram bucket estimate); investigate slow inputs or engine contention.
p99 processor latency exceeds its SLO (histogram bucket estimate).
Retry rate is elevated; a high share of attempts are being requeued (transient failures or broker blips).
Dead-letter rate is elevated; jobs are exhausting their retries and failing terminally.
The malware scanner is failing to complete scans; inputs are not processed unscanned, so the queue may back up.
Runnable queue depth is high and the backlog is not draining; scale workers or investigate stalls. Operator-fed metric.
rules.note: Requires feeding the broker's observed depth; the shipped daemon does not sample it.

rules.summary: The oldest runnable job has aged past the SLO; jobs are waiting too long to be claimed. Operator-fed metric.
Deep image compression is unavailable on the worker (no native engine); deep jobs fail honestly. Degraded, not a breach.
A verified observed bucket configuration shows the retention backstop does not hold; objects can outlive the privacy ceiling. Reconcile the drift.
